correctness.rationale: For every \(r,D,L>0\) the cover time is max of first hits of two endpoints; each resetting first-passage mean follows the Feynman–Kac boundary-value Laplace transform and renewal identity. Substitution gives the exact rational H_b(z); exact differentiation leaves a quadratic F_b in \(z^2\) with one positive root, ruling out interior minima. Endpoint differences have the sign of \(2b^2-b-2\), producing a unique global threshold; \(F_b(1)\) and \(F_b(b^2)\) classify local stability and the separate spinodal. The proof checks all equality cases, endpoints and open intervals. Symbolic algebra and 748 independent numerical/finite-difference assertions supplement the analytical proof; finite sampling is not used to infer all-parameter uniqueness.

value.rationale: Choosing where to begin and reset is a natural physical design problem for full-interval coverage: endpoints pre-satisfy one target, whereas the midpoint balances the two farthest targets. The exact first-order optimizer jump, strict exclusion of off-center global optima, distinct local-stability spinodal and metastability regime constitute a complete interpretable classification; these results are not numerical recomputation of an arbitrary table or a cheap normalization check.
